item.title: Hephaestus - SCP Concept
item.description: An SCP describing a wildfire which is not extinguishable.
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Typical Layout (SC Procedures, Description, Addenda)

Genre: No specific genre

Elevator Pitch: The SCP (Preferably SCP-5766) is a wildfire located in Northern Norway started in late April of 2010 approximately 0.43 square kilometres in area.

Central Narrative: SCP was started in late April of 2010 at 2:00 PM during a lightning storm that had killed over 200 separate creatures including foxes, wolves, reindeer, and puffins. SCP was presumably started when a lightning strike lit several coniferous trees affected by dry-rot.

SCP was discovered by a hiker during a hike in Northern Norway. At 4pm, he noticed a large quantity of soot and smoke in the trees, a noticeable change in visibility of the area and an increased air temperature. He followed what he presumed where the smoke originated from, and unknowingly discovered SCP while the large volume of smoke in the area, however he never noticed the presence of SCP.

The Foundation was first notified of SCP from the Norwegian Government when a collection of meteorologists and climatologists noticed an unusual quantity of smoke coming from the region of the SCP’s presence. The Foundation investigated and put containment of the object into effect.

SCP began forming a local greenhouse effect across its nearby regions on the 13th of September 2012, through immense emission of Carbon Dioxide and Water Vapour, causing intense heat during the day and night hours in the region.

Attention-Grabber: This SCP is the first SCP mainly focused on wildfires.

Addenda:

  • Hephaestus is the God of Fire in Greek Mythology.

item.title: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is an anomalous event in a gas station, where if an individual looks at the bathroom's mirror for enough time they will be controlled and later killed by their reflection.

Central Narrative: An SCP Foundation Researcher is driving in his car to his house, he suddenly sees a gas station and stops there to wash his face. He enters the bathroom and begins realizing this gas station was never here before, hence why he didn't recognize it. As he was washing his face, the Researcher began looking intently at the mirror and started scratching his arm uncontrollably, grabbed his hair and breathed heavily, showing signs of paranoia, then suddenly began acting against his own will and followed his reflection's movement. After a bit, the reflection smiled and grabbed a hammer, so did the Researcher, they both swung the hammer towards the mirror, shattering it, and the Staff member dropped dead in the bathroom with multiple cuts around his body. The Foundation later found the body and started studying the SCP, theorizing it's origin and it's containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The gas station is often moved between places and awaits for it's next victim, and what's interesting to note is that the individual starts becoming their own reflection and begins following it's movement. It swaps the real person with the reflection, which can't escape the mirror and can only kill others.

Additional Notes: The SCP manipulates and kills people in the same way every time, however the anomaly doesn't work if multiple people are witnessing, which is why it mostly targets one or two people. After the mirror is shattered and the individual is dead, the gas station will move locations which leaves the body on the ground in the location of the murder and rebuilds the mirror instantly.

item.title: Don't go where the stars are nebulas
item.description: SCP-XXXX is an anomaly that heavily alters the area its located it, most notably the sky.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an anomaly that alters the area it's in. It's located in the desert of Barden, Utah where there's no cities. The anomaly itself is located in an abandoned factory (although the lights of it still work for some reason) and is the body of a women shielding a child in the fetal position, with the child holding a hand-made teddy bear.

show
Hide

The body however seems to send signals that are telepathic in nature. However, the only things the foundation was able to decipher said "Please help me," and "Is my son okay?"
After the Sudden appearance of the anomaly where made, the SCP foundation attempted to contain it, but it showed ineffective as any structures made to contain it where altered or removed completely.

Central Narrative: After the sudden appearance of SCP-XXXX, the SCP foundation revived reports of cars getting into accidents where the area was altered, such as boulders suddenly appearing, roads leading to giant holes, etc. The foundation investigated and found a partially working but abandoned factory that wasn't there before. They quickly shut off the road passing by the anomaly and began investigating.

Show
Hide

Explorations in the anomaly where conducted and they found out that the mother was protecting her from something, but what that something is is unknown. The factory seemed to undergo several major failures and an outside force pushing into the factory.
The alteration in the area is discovered to be SCP-XXXX changing it to fit the area of where they came from, most likely another universe or dimension.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For readers into SCP articles with plenty of exploration logs and mystery to solve, this can be a good article for them

Additional Notes: I was considering making a "Ray Cat solution" where the scp foundation is unable to contain it entirely and instead intergrated the properties of the scp into pop-culture and warn the dangers of "where the stars turned into nebulas"

It is a 1.8 meter tall floating polyhedron figure that vibrates faster then the human eye can see, making it look distorted (I have a drawing and a sandbox, reply and ask for this if you would like.) There is no way yet found to figure out the actual shape of this SCP, but is expected to be larger then seen. It's voice is heard from all directions within a 20 foot radius, directly speaking into the mind of the listener, not from any position.

SCP also grows in size when matter is absorbed by it, depending on the mass of the object. SCP has the ability to lure in people to come in contact with it, seemingly unwillingly, which in turns gets absorbed by SCP to gain mass. (Interview). The SCP seems to be willing to stay in the containment, in fear of doing harm to the planet and its people, "I intend to cause no destruction, but my nature on this plane of existence is dangerous." (SCP).

item.title: SCP Idea: Stuffed animals
item.description: Sentient stuffed animals
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional.

Elevator Pitch: 2 plush puppies that come to life whenever a child is nearby. They act like regular puppies, but very aggressive towards any adult with a lab coat. They have no way of harming anyone.

Central Narrative: The puppies have the consciousness of 2 young kids. The kids and one of their parents were on the brink of death after an accident. While in the hospital, a doctor was testing to see if they could transfer consciousness into anything other than a computer, and used the family as test subjects. It is implied that the near-dead parent is somewhere, but has gone missing. The 2 kids are all the Foundation has so far.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I intend this to be a slow burn, of sorts. The final addendum will reveal the full story, but before that, there are clues. The pups will be afraid of the researchers and would try to protect any kid from them, one will react to their human name, they'll try to get people they trust to follow them somewhere, etc. It's a little mystery before the end of the article.

Additional Notes: While the pups wouldn't be able to talk, I am thinking about having an "interview" log of sorts, where they'd be able to point to words on a board and communicate that way. I'm not sure if that's a good idea though, so any insight will help with that!

item.title: SCP: The Tooth Jar (seeking greenlights)
item.description: Eating food next to this SCP will trigger uncanny phenomena
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an ordinary looking empty glass jar
  • If a human subject is eating a meal within a short distance radius around SCP-XXXX, teeth will appear inside the food
  • Putting these teeth inside the jar will transmute them into radioactive coins
+ Show more
- Show less

Central Narrative:

SCP-XXXX is a ordinary looking glass jar that can be opened or closed with a metallic lid. Manufacturing codes engraved at the bottom of SCP-XXXX suggest it originally was a jar of Dijon mustard.

Eating solid food within a 20 meter radius around SCP-XXXX will have the following effect occur: after chewing four to five times, the subject will bite on a small human tooth, that was not initially present in the food. This tooth, called SCP-XXXX-1, matches the DNA of the subject that bit on it, although no loss of tooth is observed on the subject.

This phenomenon can be repeated. An instance of SPC-XXXX-1 will appear in the consumed food every four to five mastications, and this will always result in the subject biting onto it, leading to possible mouth injuries if unprepared.
Every time an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 is created, its mass is substracted from the subject's bone mass. Excessive repetition of the phenomenon on the same subject will result in the onset of bone-related diseases, such as osteoporosis.

Placing instances of SCP-XXXX-1 into SCP-XXXX, closing it with the lid, and breaking all visual contact with it allow for the transmutation event to take place instantly.
The transmutation event can occur only if no human person or camera has a visual contact with SCP-XXXX. The transmutation effectively replaces all instances of SCP-XXXX-1 with coins, referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-2 look identical to coins of the French Franc currency. Composition and engravings on the surface matches that of regular coins melted in 1982.
All instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are highly radioactive, averaging 80 μSv/h, warranting their rapid disposal.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Have you ever bitten on your own dislodged tooth while eating, when you were a child? It's not the most pleasant of sensations. This SCP also twists the tale of the tooth fairy in a SCP-esque fashion.

item.description: A being/object made up of all light and a little matter.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Mystery)

Page Layout (Optional): A slightly more modernized version of a regular file entry/document, with the tests and interviews all in a recording log form.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This SCP looks different to everyone who sees it.
  • Once someone sees it, they always see it that way.
  • Once seen it can never be forgotten not even by the top class amnestics.

Central Narrative: The artist who made the painting had went missing a few months before the object was found. Whoever made it and it's purpose is unknown. It may have a pocket dimension and that's where it gets all of it's "forms" from. This SCP has fooled the foundation for years, got a little carried away one time and was reclassified and containment procedures became way more strict. It also knows more than anyone thinks, It knows stuff that seems like it was just made up. But most of the time it actually happened.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP was found in an abandoned house, full of pictures and drawings. It seemed to belong to a an enthusiastic artist. Despite it's very silent nature, it has been proven to be sentient. When the SCP rarely does talk, it doesn't talk much and keeps to itself. It's more cunning and deceptive than some top deception artists. It's like creativity itself, but it is not the easiest to persuade to do anything willingly.

Additional Notes: I'd like more help with the Hook/Attention Grabber and Central Narrative. I am not too good at figuring out what info should go in which spot, so I'd like help with that.

item.title: The Serpent
item.description: A snake that can consume and manipulate DNA to grow any life form from an unknown type of plant that it created
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a giant snake in golden skin that has ability to grow an unknown type of plants in surrounding area that is capable of producing any life form/part of the life form based on the DNA and the nutrients that SCP-XXXX consumed (the DNA can only be stored inside the SCP for a few months). It is capable of twisting and manipulating the DNA although it's not good at doing so. After the incident, the SCP foundation found out that SCP-XXXX can also manipulate its own organic structure and DNA. Because of experiments with many type of life form and other anomolies SCP-XXXX became highly sapient with some other abilities:
• When in an effective range any action that is carried out with the intent to kill SCP-XXXX is impossible to do
• Ability to read anyone mind in a range
• After self-cannibalism, SCP-XXXX heal, slightly change appearance and create time distortion (time moves unevenly, some areas slow, some fast and even stopped or skip appart. Seemingly it can control all of that) around itself for a few hours

Central Narrative: due to the nature of SCP-XXXX , the foundation decided to use it to create loyal anomolies that can help the foundation in containing other SCPs. The foundation tried to understand and control SCP-XXXX. After many attempt, the foundation aware of the changes in behavior and decided to cancel the project. A failed termination attempt caused a severe damage to the site, for some reason SCP-XXXX stayed inside a site and created a person that could understand it. He later become a researcher level 3 and one of the lead researcher in containing SCP-XXXX

Hook/Attention-Grabber: it is interesting to think about the possibility of what can this SCP do, what happens if it interact with other organic SCPs. The other thing that make this special is that the contradictions between the fact that this SCP poses a huge threat to humanity and the fact that it needs the foundation

item.title: A Day in the Life *Seeking Greenlights*
item.description: Budgetary assessment detailing an unusual labor cost issue stemming from psychiatric difficulties with general staff.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: Tale.

Genre: Bureaucratic slice-of-life.

Page Layout: Presented as an in-universe section of the Quarterly Foundation Budgetary Assessment.

Elevator Pitch: Accountants and actuaries would be a vital part of the Foundation infrastructure that is often handwaved away. This tale would serve to highlight their role in the background of the narrative, considering the cost and risk-benefit analyses inherent in any large-scale organization.

Central Narrative: Menial workers (janitors, maintenance technicians, etc.) in contact with various low-danger anomalies begin to display mental ailments not consistent with any prior anomalous traits. Pre-existing case studies of various examples are presented. An across-the-board complete neurological and psychiatric evaluation is proposed in order to fully grasp the scope of the issue. O5 Command agrees, but also prescribed an analysis of replacing potentially compromised staff with genetically engineered automata.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The format itself is different than what typically appears; the concern for fiscal resources is also generally not present in-universe. Additionally, describing the toll that most "normal" Foundation staff must pay in their line of duty: having to constantly refer to a rose bush by a different, feminine name; be inundated with the color red, not only at work, but in the rest of their lives; even the burden of having to clean the tank of a sea slug that speaks to you and claims to be a renowned naturalist. Finally, the concept of replacing people with organic AIs is presented with the cold, classically-Foundation disregard for the livelihood and general concern of the people.

item.title: Phantom Entry
item.description: An anomalous Security Containment Procedure entry in the foundation's database, suddenly appearing out of nowhere.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional, Comedy, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: An SCP entry about an anomalous SCP entry.

Central Narrative: Out of nowhere, a new fully authorized SCP entry has appeared randomly in the Foundation's database, where it describes an entity so foreign and alien to the current local reality, where any and all sophisticated informational stimuli regarding it cannot be transcribed and comprehended when unaided, resulting in the immediate loss of said information after it removes its presence, such as memory. Translations, however, are perfectly comprehensible, such as written or recorded materials. However, it may also be corrupted if said entity acts upon it. The entity refers to itself in the English language as "Your Warden" or "Them", a being that proclaimed itself as the safe keeper of all reality from itself, by destroying realities beyond repair, and cleaning those near broken. However, even with all the SCP shenanigans, the time it spent observing the world(s) in this local reality had changed its mind, and coming to the absurd conclusion that the SCP universe may be the most convoluted, but it is far from broken, and everything belongs, resulting in its departure leaving this reality to its own business.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mass confusion where absolutely no one remembers anything regarding the Security Containment Procedure ever transpiring adds to the curiosity of the reader, and it also enjoys the treatment of a drastic mood change, it slowly shifts from being a lighthearted slice of life reality hopping Mary Sue into a dreadful, cosmic horror-esque atmosphere. The horror will be mostly informational horror, the feeling of dread when presented absurd consensuses and information. There's just too much out there, and you have no say over it. The struggle to understand will lead to hatred, fear, confusion, denial, and much more will be explored.

item.title: SCP-6285 - The Putrefaction - Seeking Greenlit
item.description: A contagious fungus that is able to raise the dead.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Action, Drama

Elevator Pitch:

+) It is a contagious fungus that is capable of raising the dead, then after a particular time, the now living dead will grow extra sharp bones out of their body, particularly the limbs. The reason being that having sharp "weapons" is the most useful way for SCP-6285-1 (The corpses) to kill other living humans which spreads the infection even further. The fungus shoots out spores and coming into contact with human corpses will begin to reanimate them. If there is a living human around there, it will attach to them as transportation without them knowing.

+) The unpredictable neverending evolution and mutation of the fungus is what makes it so deadly. This means SCP-6285-1 can have limitless potential and growth to serve the fungus's purpose.

+) SCP-6285-1 also has an invisible gooey substance which helps to patch its wounds if necessary. Using extreme heat is the best way to neutralize it.

Central Narrative: It should be from going normal, peaceful to a hell hole. At first, the SCP seems harmless and all, as time goes by, the horror and dreadfulness of it will soon come cause of how infectious it can spread and fast reanimation

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Putrefaction is unique in terms of reanimating the dead if this is a thing. To be honest, I was inspired by the Necromorphs in Dead Space to that the host growing extra limbs because it is the most helpful tactic to rank up more kills for the fungus to raise an army. The terrifying existence of the fungus can cause human extinction.

item.title: {Seeking Greenlight} The Devil You Know
item.description: Beats the Devil you don't.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird

Elevator Pitch: Anyone who directly observes subject through sight or sound is suddenly and unwaveringly convinced the source is from a long-forgotten friend or lover they remember fondly, regardless whether said witnesses has any actual history with subject. The subject's evocative aura actively alters or erases previous experiences in their minds to replace them with its own interpretations, leading many victims to become near obsessed with the entity after extended periods. Subject has potential to teleport near anyone previously exposed to its anomalous presence, manifesting instantaneously around corners or behind doors.

+ Negating Other Mind-Affecting Anomalies
- Hide

The most notable and bizarre feature to this process, however, is that continued exposure to the subject's anomalous presence can completely eliminate any pre-existing mental manipulative affects placed upon any human’s mind. For example, if another anomalous effect from another SCP-recorded creature infects their victim's mind with permanent delusions or extreme abnormal behavior, prolonged and repeated exposure to this subject's presence through conversation can remedy these effects. Required intervals of exposure necessary to perform this ranges from days to years, depending on how powerful said previous mental afflictions were.

Central Narrative: The entity was borne out of an unknown man’s own sacrifice to ritualistically create something from the collective unconscious of humanity; unfortunately considered a failure, as a tether connected human consciousness remains attached. Subject finds mild entertainment in playing with the strings of human minds, observing them as charming yet fickle and simplistic instruments of manipulation. Anomalous effects are second-nature and hardly intentional, though also has an intuitive understanding to read human emotions with 100% accuracy from its direct connection to human consciousness that was not severed during its creation. It rarely expresses any strong emotions, however grows more compelled to assist the foundation in efforts to either understand or combat other mind-affecting anomalies, considering them a threat or challenge to its domain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature can be dangerous due to its addictive aura and teleportative capabilities, but the utilization of said anomalous properties to counteract active influence of other mind-affecting SCP creatures can be an invaluable asset.

Tags: auditory, compulsion, cognitohazard, empathetic, humanoid, mind-affecting, keter, sapient, sentient, teleportation, visual

item.title: Snatcher Slug (Seeking Critique)
item.description: My first SCP, currently seeking critique and maybe a greenlight, but not quite yet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Not yet

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an SCP that can attach itself to a host, designated SCP-XXXX-1, in the form of a small slug that slowly feeds off of its host until the host is completely alone from anyone else and is isolated somewhere where it can not be detected killing them. It then pumps a potent, instantly acting neurotoxin into their bloodstream and assimilates as them, eating them for nutrition. SCP-XXXX then goes around as SCP-XXXX-1, designated as -2 from that point. It releases more small instances of SCP-XXXX that repeat the process, and after a period of two years, -2 dies. SCP-XXXX can infect any sufficiently complex organism, and inherits all abilities of that organism. It has been observed assimilating with dogs, cats, and even a juvenile Kokomo dragon. A definite way to detect -2 is to take a Copper or Gold wire heated to at least 15° Celsius and submerge it lightly in a blood sample of -2. When the wire touches the blood, it jumps away. Containing it is somewhat difficult, as it can assimilate into anyone and can not be killed with regular firearms. Instead, to permanently destroy or severely incapacitate it requires using incendiary weaponry. It can survive in pretty much any environment, but to contain it, there is a small room, where over the course of a day, 12 gallons of pig's blood is pumped in for XXXX. The room has 14 different cameras with overlapping sight lines. Past that room is an airlock where there are flamethrower countermeasures installed and infrared scanners to detect the abnormally high body temperature of XXXX.

Central Narrative: A Foundation Research team of twelve researchers are moving to investigate an odd increase in the electromagnetic pulses emanating from the South Pole. They find a large asteroid buried under some ice that seems to have been there for at least 120.000 years, unearthed by melting ice. The team takes back a large canister filled with slugs back to Site-118 for study, but the organisms assimilate with them and manage to destroy the base. MTF Upsilon-6 "Cold Shoulder" (I couldn't find an MTF Squadron with the description I needed so I made one up) attempts to retrieve the scientists, unknowingly bringing back instances of -2 to Site-29, which spreads the infection of XXXX. It is recaptured and contained at Site-29, where the slugs are contained.

item.content:encoded:
The creator of all spiders. Her broken heart has left her with no ill will towards mankind left to give. My first attempt at an article.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Not yet.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: haven't settled on one yet

Elevator Pitch: A Euclid-class queen of spiders that was saddened by humanity's cruelty towards her children to the point where her heart literally cracked. Because of this, she's surprisingly passive. She can make new species of spiders (both normal and anomalous) at will, and spiders flock to her.

Narrative Pitch: Though she has waged several wars against humanity in the past due to the mistreatment of her children that got fiercer as time went on, her heart eventually cracked, flushing all hatred from her body in a single moment. All that was left behind was sorrow.

+ show block
– hide block

Sorrow for her fallen children, and sorrow for sending her children to die in who knows how many wars that they never won. So she packed her things and left the mainland, retreating to an island. Many, many years later, the foundation responds to a radio signal from a battleship claiming that they were being attacked by an enormous spider. It's revealed that she created this spider as a guardian for her personal island that she sends out if she senses that people with bad intentions are coming to her island. The foundation does its thing, making the island as secret as possible while trying to study the spider queen. Eventually, the foundation manages to conduct some interviews with her.

Hook: Aside from the aforementioned interviews, which reveal her backstory, this SCP should be interesting among the other spider-based SCPs that she's not immediately hostile to people. There should also be implications that some of the spider-based SCPs the foundation keeps tabs on are relics of these ancient wars fought by her.

Additional Notes: While she has potential, I want to hear your input for how I could improve her concept.

item.title: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification
item.description: Short tale expansion for SCP-5118.
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/deathbygin-2

A short tale for my authored article SCP-5118.

Spoiler / Explanation
Minimize

As Dr. Atmos gather information from Dr. Williams, it's implied that SCP-5118 is actually a dog who is a reality bender, turned human, and turned back into a dog when about to be captured. Evidence to support this includes:

  • SCP-5118 did not act like most other reality benders do when discovering they have powers (usually by hiding them from others).
  • SCP-5118 manifests chocolate, grapes, and soda - all things a dog cannot eat.
  • SCP-5118 appeared to be smiling while being chased.
  • SCP-5118 does not attempt to breach containment because it's current living situation is already ideal (it gets a bed, new toys, guaranteed food and water, and socializes with staff daily when they provide it with food).
  • Using it's powers while in containment would risk exposing itself. Since it's implied that it's "original form" is already a dog, the scans / tests from the SCP article would show nothing.

I wanted to write this tale to add a twist to the article without making this the clear-cut canon. Please let me know what you think.

item.title: Irish Fairies
item.description: [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
Irish Fairies, fay creatures that toy and manipulate with humans physically and mentally.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that the SCPs are based on Irish fairies, who are (in short) tricksters who manipulate humans in various ways. Whether that be by manipulating their mind to go crazy or manipulating their body to disform them. Fairies were blamed for various things in medieval Ireland, some of those include stuff like schizophrenia or disabilities being 'curses' from fairies. The SCP will differ from generic fairies by being inherently malevolent when the original fairies are not.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: After various missing person reports, and the discovery of a body missing a symmetrical hole in their chest, the Foundation investigate a forest in Ireland. While investigating, one of the team starts hearing voices telling them to kill their teammates and to 'come to the festival' upon telling the team of this the MTF, assuming the SCP has something to do with this, detain and amnestisize the teammate. They leave one MTF to bring the affected teammate out of the forest to safety and continue. After a bit, the MTF see various colorful lights in the distance, and they all begin to hear voices telling them to 'come to the festival'. At this point, the MTF stop broadcasting their video and we are left with only their audio. The captain, who appears to be the least affected, describes what's happening while the others start going mad. Eventually, the captain attempts to flee the situation at which various etheral screaming can be heard before he goes offline.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Well I tried my best to make sure it leaves a lot of questions, and the fact that it's a twist on what is normally considered cute or harmless is pretty interesting.

Additional Notes: I don't know how I feel about the narrative (which is why I'm not seeking a greenlight yet), so I would like critisicm to be focused on that.

item.title: SCP Idea Whale Eating Bird
item.description: A giant bird that hunts whales, based off of the Thunderbird cryptid. My first attempt at an article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No, at least not yet.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre:I haven't settled on one yet, though it will likely be action/suspense.

Layout: Information presentation

Elevator Pitch: A Keter class giant bird, living on an island in the Pacific, hunting whales like an osprey. Unnaturally large and fast, it occasionally attacks human ships.

Central Narrative: The Foundation deploys operatives to the North Pacific after a large bird attacks a group of whale watchers. After some investigation, they are unable to find anything, but stay posted. A few years later, a surfaced Soviet Submarine is sunk by the creature. The Foundation ramps up the search, eventually tracking it to a remote island between Chile and New Zealand. A submarine is sent to drop off a scout crew, but the sub is sunk because they underestimate how deep the creature can dive. A cruiser is deployed, and fires upon the creature when it attempts to dive at it. The bird survives, but the mission is called off to avoid potentially killing it. Another sub is deployed, this time equipped with an improved diving system to get down faster, and more ships surrounding the area to track it by RADAR. The crew treks up the small dormant volcanic island, and finds a nest made of logs with scattered bones. When the RADAR team radios them to say that the bird is returning home, they quickly find that it is coming faster than expected, and the submarine that they arrived on is unable to pick them up. They are forced to spend a night on the island with the bird, but it barely acknowledges them. It is determined that the creature is not a threat, and will be contained simply by baiting it away from coasts and sea lanes.

Hook: The Special Containment Procedure stands out compared to the SCPs I've read. The bird itself isn't dangerous enough to warrant destruction, and generally isolates itself. The Foundation would figure that it's more worthwhile to monitor it, and keep the thing away from humans.

This is my first Article, so I'm a bit nervous about it. Also, I'm aware that there is already a "Thunderbird" Article, but the concept for this one is completely different.

item.content:encoded:
A new humanoid, Euclid-class SCP, who might be Cain and Abel's sibling.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX, AKA the Red Girl, is a humanoid anomaly which takes the appearance of a 15-16 year old girl with with long hair and irises in a unnatural shade of bright red. The Red Girl shows usually sweet, affective behavior, but will get triggered if she gets visually or audibly exposed to rage or hatred, or senses rage in a nearby person. SCP-XXXX will undergo a rapid transformation, in which she grows red scales on 60% of her body, will grow claws and fangs and the hair will turn into spikes. SCP-XXXX will then attempt to viciously attack the person that it sensed the anger from, often resulting in a chain reaction if multiple people are nearby, although it will never attack more than 8 people in a row. After the attack, SCP-XXXX will show shock and remorse over its own deeds, and slowly regain her human appearance. Attempts learn SCP-XXXX to control this states have proven ineffective, as the Red Girl seems to lose all memories of the incident within the next 8 hours.

Central Narrative: Although the origins of SCP-XXXX are unbeknownst even to her, Foundation researchers have found one potential clue: on the left shoulder blade, SCP-XXXX bears a tattoo of Sumerian origin, meaning 3 in the original language. This might be a link to SCP-073, who carries a similar mark on his body. Some researchers even started to reference to SCP-XXXX as 'the third sibling', although further research will be necessary before a link can be confirmed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I want to expand the concepts of SCP-073 and SCP-076. Wouldn't it be interesting to see what would happen if it gets confirmed that Cain and Abel in the SCP universe have a younger sister, who possesses yet another set of anomalous abilities, alongside resemblance in personalities from both brothers?

item.title: The Hungry Constellation
item.description: A shape-shifting constellation that can give anomalous properties
item.content:encoded:
A shape-shifting constellation that can give anomalous properties to whatever it 'eats' based on a two-dimensional perspective from a specific observer

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

The anomaly is a constellation that can take the shape of any Earth-like creature that has a mouth that can be displayed easily in two-dimensions from a perspective, say, a beak. The anomaly is inactive by default, but can be activated for a while if a selected group of people see it, a group which I haven't decided on yet. Once activated, the jaws or beaks or etc. of the constellation closes very slowly, and anything that is 'inside' the jaw relative to the observer from the group of people is destroyed.

In a nutshell, a constellation that gets hungry when a select observer from a group of people sees it.

item.title: They Just Keep Searching
item.description: Seeking critique and possible greenlights for my first SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I posted this one before, but that was well over two weeks ago and it didn't get any responses. Figured I might as well try this forum again before looking into other critique options :) (I have made some very slight modifications since, anyway).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make heavy use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 10 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Eventually these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and high resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Will search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP idea so I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away! I'm still trying to think of a better name for it.

item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Occurs over several iterations, with the threat increasing over time

+ View Block

Elevator Pitch: - A memetic effect which can be transferred through print, speech, or digital media.

-The infection causes all infected individuals to begin speaking in an info-hazardous language. Every 2 days infected individuals will become paralysed for an increasing period of time. Within 7 months this paralysis will become permanent.

-Individuals affected by the anomaly will be conscious during the period of paralysis, being somehow disconnected from their body and walking around in an incorporeal form. Within this form, they will be unable to communicate with any other affected individuals or non-affected individuals. When in this form, a massive black obelisk, which called Iskententhine (translating to 'That which is the end)

-Affected individuals are unaware of the memetic basis of their infection unless told, and as such are likely to speak to everyone as if speaking in normal English.

Central Narrative: -Anomaly is first thought to be safe, as an anomaly affecting the population of a factory near a city that doesn't exist (this is important), but soon is reclassified as Euclid as several foundation researchers and D-Class are infected (The Euclid level object is a new iteration). The foundation researchers are amneticised [[footnote]] This is spelled wrong]] and contained, but it is believed that one infection gets out, as the infection reappears in the high school where a researchers son lives.

-Object is re-classified as Keter after the infection is thought to be neutralised by aggressive foundation action, and efforts to bury all affected individuals. The effect re-appears in several different locations following this, and soon large swaths of humanity are infected. Several prominent foundation members move into secure facilities to wait out the disaster. SCP-2000 is activated, the foundation recommends suicide for all individuals and efforts from several Groups of interests create a 1km layer of dirt and dust over the original earth, creating new geological formations. Shortly after, the O5 leave the containment chamber, recreate humanity, and continue.

The final iterations object class is Cernunnos, and it seems that the infection has arisen again, in Site 102, Canberra, Australia.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Will the foundation sacrifice human communication permanently to save humanity?

Notes: I had a wildly different idea under the same name previously. This article is completely different from that (the only thing in common is the hook), so I've put it in a new thread.

item.title: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.description: An anomalous and dangerous creature lurks in the depths of the Atlantic,
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is large, dark, quadrupedal aquatic lifeform located somewhere in the Atlantic at a site known as The Ring. SCP can only viewed at night at designated platforms 350m below sea level. Videoing or photographing SCP-XXXX must be avoided as well as viewing it for more than 1 minute continuously, or making direct eye contact.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was first alerted to the SCP foundation through a field agent located inside of NOAA. NOAA identified a drastic change in salinity in an area roughly 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Field Agents Smith, Jones, Roger, Greeves and Alex investigated the site of this anomalous activity using a SCP ship Horizon. Upon arrival the agents confirmed a change in salinity within the area as well as mutated and aggressive versions of the local fauna and flora. All agents sent to investigate this anomalous area during this initial Expedition, never returned. The last contact with the foundation in the transcript logs ended with the lead agent Smith saying:

"It's in the water, its in my head, its on the boat… send Deep Feeders"
After a considerable loss of life and 3 more expeditions were the foundation able to secure SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is capable Phycological Physical Mutation creating a sub entity of various forms like the Gespenst( wraith). SCP is also capable of salinity conversion, which if left uncheck can cause cataclysmic change in weather, flora/fauna, disrupt oxygen levels.

Additional Notes:Constructive criticism is greatly appreciated.👍

item.title: The Painter (Old Concept)
item.description: He is the judge that shall decide the fate of humans, you cannot escape your own fate.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Elevator Pitch: The Painter is a faceless humanoid male with little to no facial features, the exception being it's eyes, it is able to decide the (horrible and gruesome) fate of any living human by painting it on a canvas (fate as in the way they die). No matter how hard it's victims will try they will always meet their fate, this manipulates the world around the victim so that they will meet their fate no matter the cost, it's only limitation is that it must know how the victim looks like in order to put them on a canvas. The foundation is unable to take the paintbrush and the canvas of the Painter because it's own fate is to keep painting until the end of mankind itself, so any attempt in doing so will result in an inevitable failure because there will always be a series of unstoppable events that will result in the painter getting it's necessary tools for it to continue painting.

Central Narrative: The Painter's story is that it is the judge of humanity, it is here to create and manipulate everyone's fate, it decides how and when everyone will experience their final moments and it will not stop until everyone's fate is set. The foundation also needs to severely restrict the painter's knowledge of any other SCPs, just imagine the damage if it were to paint a scientist in the jaws of 682, a huge containment breach would have to happen in order for the scientist to meet their fate.

The Painter was originally found in a cabin in the woods after a few campers reported "a weird man painting them dying in horrible ways". After a few years all of the campers died exactly how they reported the paintings to look like and that's when the foundation stepped in, they used smoke grenades, thermal vision and a bag to blind the target and capture it, but being captured by the foundation was only part of it's fate, it will use the foundation's infinite resources in order to keep painting.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will contain a few of the many victims of the Painter and how they met their grim fate, how the foundation will conduct tests on the painter and how it's anomalous world manipulation effect had a change on the world and the foundation.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea, my first one actually, I made an old thread about it almost a year ago and I'm trying to revisit the concept and improve it. hopefully I will be able to achieve that, if you decide to visit the old thread and find that you like the original concept more or some ideas from it, just let me know.

item.title: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Greenlights)
item.description: Anomalous section of California coastline
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article. Name, Classification, Containment procedures, description.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a beach sixty miles south of Long Beach, California upon which, no matter how far on walks, the water can never be reached, yet always appears to be no more than eighty to ninety yards away.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Through audio logs between expeditionary personnel and command, readers will follow teams of research personnel sent to explore SCP-XXXX in hopes to discover more about its anomalous nature. The first audio log reveals initial exploration results in a casualty around eight km out. Autopsy reveals cause of death to be asphyxia by drowning. The second log reveals that use of a SCBA allows explorers to venture out substantially farther, reaching close to sixteen kilometers before oxygen tanks reach half-way empty and they must turn around. The third log follows a team of researchers equipped with oxygen tanks that last eighteen hours. The team reports around thirty km out that there is some form of writing in the sand. Later, they report what they believe to be a boat in the distance, floating offshore. At thirty-nine km, three of the oxygen tanks simultaneously malfunction. The team turns around, holding their breath unless breathing through the SCBA, which they must share. All team members are recovered, and the writing in the sand is sent to linguists for deciphering. The final log documents the exploration of four research personnel on board a semi-aquatic vehicle designed to withstand high pressure and impact. They make it twenty-six km before the vehicle begins to flood with water. The team is forced to abandon the vehicle and carry on. At the fifty-seven km mark, the lead researcher calls in that there appears to be a tall, disproportionate figure down near the water, henceforth denoted as SCP-XXXX-1. Before command can respond, all exploration personnel experience simultaneous SCBA failures, and the hissing of air and screaming of researchers can be heard before comm connection is lost. Three of the four corpses are recovered and autopsied, and cause of death is determined to be asphyxia by drowning. The fourth cable comes back severed, and there is blood and a torn shred of clothing on the cable.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dry-drowning premise is unique and the audio logs will serve to keep readers interested.

Additional Notes: Researchers in the audio logs are tethered by spools of steel cable so they can be recovered. Feedback still welcome.
